## #247 after-deploy performance receipt

Merge: `88636516859d2249548920c9e7aaadc53b5178a5` (merged 2026-11-19T00:52:21Z). Measured live daemon reports commit `8863651685`, PID **61945** in both pings. This completes the owed after-deploy measurement; the held-close memory-note scenario is still the separate upcoming live proof.

Command (exit 0):
```sh
date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ
pij-rs --json ping
just spawn-rate --seconds 20
date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ
pij-rs --json ping
/bin/ps -p 61945 -o pid=,%cpu=,rss=,etime=,command=
```

Pair boundary timestamps: **2026-11-19T00:54:05Z → 00:54:26Z**; sampler reports **20.0 s**, command wall time 20.35 s. Exact daemon spawn total **428 → 428**: **zero launches** between pings. Every by_op value is unchanged:

| gh.delivered | 1 | 1 |
| git.community | 7 | 7 |
| ps.registration-native-process | 149 | 149 |
| ps.sidecar-process-group | 1 | 1 |
| tmux.control-client | 1 | 1 |
| tmux.pipe-pane attach | 130 | 130 |
| tmux.rename-window | 3 | 3 |
| tmux.set-options tap owner | 130 | 130 |

### Before / after on the same live machine

| Measurement | Before deploy | After deploy |
|---|---:|---:|
| Daemon PID | 23167 | 61945 |
| Daemon commit | 577a6c7a13 | 8863651685 |
| Exact daemon launches during pair | 1 | 0 |
| Exact daemon launch rate | 0.05/s | 0/s |
| Whole-machine new processes | 186.2/s | 168.1/s |
| Sampled processes | 164.7/s | 164.2/s |
| Sampler polls | 137563 | 137071 |
| `ps` daemon CPU | 18.2% | 69.2% |
| Daemon RSS | 165712 KiB | 223440 KiB |
| Daemon elapsed at resource snapshot | 36:28 | 00:48 |

Before window: 00:37:28Z–00:37:48Z; its sole exact daemon increment was `git.pa-watchdog-common-dir` 28→29. After sampler attribution lower bounds: gone-before-seen 112.1/s, other 52.1/s; no daemon children observed; statusline runs 0.0/s; Claude display/stop hooks 0.0/s. Per-parent sampling is a lower bound; the exact counter is the daemon launch receipt.

**Reading:** no added daemon process launches observed in the deployed window. The machine total is lower, but workload was not controlled and this does not establish a causal PR improvement. CPU and RSS are **higher**, not improved: the after snapshot is a 48-second-old daemon versus the baseline's 36-minute-old daemon, and `ps %cpu` is not a matched interval benchmark. Startup/workload attribution is unproven; do not interpret this as steady-state CPU/RSS equivalence. Neither this launch sampler nor its CPU snapshot measures the reduction in activity HTTP posts directly.

Performance source verdict remains pass-with-notes: settle retargets the existing per-pending-turn deadline, no new polling task; grace adds per-close state and a normally in-process process-start probe (existing counted `/bin/ps` fallback remains). No local build/test was run. No memory note has been written before the requested close proof.
